# Functions {-}

```{r echo=FALSE}
## Define  interaction table functions {-}

compact_emm_table <- function(emm_object,
                              by_var,
                              condition_prefix = NULL,
                              reverse = FALSE,      # TRUE = later level minus earlier (revpairwise)
                              adjust = NULL,        # NULL = emmeans default; e.g. "none", "tukey", "holm"
                              digits_est = 2,
                              digits_df = 1,
                              digits_p = 3,
                              digits_by = 2) {      # decimals shown for numeric by-values (e.g. OS, LP)

  emm_df <- summary(emm_object) |> as.data.frame()

  # by_var can be one bare name (by_var = OS) or several (by_var = c(family_size, OS))
  by_names <- names(tidyselect::eval_select(rlang::enquo(by_var), emm_df))

  contrast_df <- if (is.null(adjust)) {
    pairs(emm_object, reverse = reverse)
  } else {
    pairs(emm_object, reverse = reverse, adjust = adjust)
  }
  contrast_df <- contrast_df |> summary() |> as.data.frame()

  # Exclude BOTH Satterthwaite/KR-style and asymptotic-style CI/df column names
  non_focal_cols <- c(by_names, "emmean", "SE", "df",
                      "lower.CL", "upper.CL",
                      "asymp.LCL", "asymp.UCL")
  focal_vars <- setdiff(names(emm_df), non_focal_cols)

  # Detect whichever CI column names are actually present
  lcl_col <- intersect(c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"), names(emm_df))
  ucl_col <- intersect(c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"), names(emm_df))

  # Condition label: a bare value (single by-variable, no prefix, as before),
  # "prefix = value" (single by-variable with prefix), or
  # "name = value, name = value" (several by-variables)
  fmt_by <- function(x) {
    if (is.numeric(x)) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits_by) else as.character(x)
  }
  make_condition <- function(df) {
    if (length(by_names) == 1) {
      v <- fmt_by(df[[by_names]])
      if (is.null(condition_prefix)) v else paste(condition_prefix, "=", v)
    } else {
      parts <- lapply(by_names, function(n) paste(n, "=", fmt_by(df[[n]])))
      do.call(paste, c(parts, sep = ", "))
    }
  }

  emm_part <- emm_df |>
    rowwise() |>
    mutate(Comparison = paste(c_across(all_of(focal_vars)), collapse = " ")) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(Condition = make_condition(pick(everything()))) |>
    transmute(
      across(all_of(by_names)),          # kept temporarily for sorting
      Comparison,
      Condition,
      Estimate = emmean,
      SE,
      df,
      lower.CL = if (length(lcl_col) > 0) .data[[lcl_col]] else NA_real_,
      upper.CL = if (length(ucl_col) > 0) .data[[ucl_col]] else NA_real_,
      t.ratio = NA_real_,
      p.value = NA_real_
    )

  # Detect whichever test-statistic column name is present (t.ratio vs z.ratio)
  ratio_col <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(contrast_df))

  contrast_part <- contrast_df |>
    mutate(Comparison = as.character(contrast),
           Condition  = make_condition(pick(everything()))) |>
    transmute(
      across(all_of(by_names)),
      Comparison,
      Condition,
      Estimate = estimate,
      SE,
      df,
      lower.CL = NA_real_,
      upper.CL = NA_real_,
      t.ratio = if (length(ratio_col) > 0) .data[[ratio_col]] else NA_real_,
      p.value
    )

  # Sort by the by-variables' actual values (numeric order for OS/LP, level
  # order for factors), not by the text label, then drop them
  bind_rows(emm_part, contrast_part) |>
    arrange(across(all_of(by_names)), Comparison) |>
    select(-all_of(by_names)) |>
    mutate(
      Estimate = round(Estimate, digits_est),
      SE       = round(SE, digits_est),
      df       = round(df, digits_df),
      lower.CL = round(lower.CL, digits_est),
      upper.CL = round(upper.CL, digits_est),
      t.ratio  = round(t.ratio, digits_est),
      p.value  = round(p.value, digits_p)
    )
}


```


# Load Files

```{r load_files, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Load data: erp_fs nonwords
erp_fs_nw <- read_csv("erp_fs_dmg.csv") |>
  filter(lexical_status == "nonword") |>
  mutate(
    SubjID = factor(SubjID),
    chlabel = factor(chlabel),
    family_size = factor(family_size, 
                         levels = c("small", "large")),
    complexity = factor(complexity,
                    levels = c("simple", "complex")),
    time_window = factor(time_window),
    OS = as.numeric(Dim.2),
    LP = as.numeric(Dim.1)
  )

range(erp_fs_nw$OS, na.rm = TRUE)
```



# N400 NONWORD DATA : SYMMETRICAL MODEL, INTERACTION WITH LP AND OS

For the nonword N400, does the symmetric model we just ran replace the separate LP and OS models, or do all three get reported?**

The symmetric model is the cleanest solution — it tests both dimensions in the same model and provides the strongest evidence for the dissociation. The separate models are now superseded.

## N400 NONWORD DATA: Family Size

### Model Comparisons
```{r}
contrasts(erp_fs_nw$complexity)   <- c(-0.5, 0.5)
contrasts(erp_fs_nw$family_size)  <- c(-0.5, 0.5)

# Full four-way
m_full_nw_n400_fs <- lmer(
  value ~ complexity * family_size * LP * OS +
    (1 | SubjID) + (1 | SubjID:chlabel),
  data = subset(erp_fs_nw, time_window == "N400"),
  REML = TRUE,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

print(summary(m_full_nw_n400_fs), correlation = TRUE)

# Effect Sizes
eta_squared(m_full_nw_n400_fs, partial = TRUE)

# R-squared
r2_nakagawa(m_full_nw_n400_fs)
```




```{r}
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)
library(rlang)
library(purrr)

emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 20000)

# Representative levels: mean ± 1 SD for both continuous ID dimensions
subj <- erp_fs_nw |>
  distinct(SubjID, OS, LP) |>
  filter(!is.na(OS), !is.na(LP))

nrow(subj)   # should be 63

os_vals <- mean(subj$OS) + c(-1, 0, 1) * sd(subj$OS)
lp_vals <- mean(subj$LP) + c(-1, 0, 1) * sd(subj$LP)
os_labels <- c("Low OS", "Mean OS", "High OS")
lp_labels <- c("Low LP", "Mean LP", "High LP")

os_vals
lp_vals
```


## Complexity × Family Size × OS (three-way, p = .047)

```{r}
# Complexity effect (complex - simple) within each family size, at each OS level
n400_fs_3way_OS_2 <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity | family_size * OS,
                             at = list(OS = os_vals, LP = lp_vals[2]), nesting = NULL) |>
  compact_emm_table(by_var = c(family_size, OS), reverse = TRUE)
as.tibble(n400_fs_3way_OS_2) |> print(n = 50)

# Gives ((complex − simple) for large) minus ((complex − simple) for small)
n400_fs_3way_OS_2b <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity * family_size | OS,
                              at = list(OS = os_vals, LP = lp_vals[2]), nesting = NULL) |>
  contrast(interaction = "revpairwise") |>
  as.data.frame() 
as.tibble(n400_fs_3way_OS_2b) |> print(n = 50)

# Gives the OS slope for complex nonwords minus the OS slope for simple nonwords, within each family size. 
# That difference is the Complexity × OS interaction at that family size. 
emtrends(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity | family_size, var = "OS") |> contrast("revpairwise")

# Gives the large-family complexity slope difference minus the small-family complexity slope difference
emtrends(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity * family_size, var = "OS",
         at = list(LP = lp_vals[2])) |>
  contrast(interaction = "revpairwise")
```


```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# N400 nonwords: Complexity x Family Size x OS
# Requires: m_full_nw_n400_fs (REML fit) and erp_fs_nw from your Rmd
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 20000)

# Participant-level OS scores (one row per participant, not per observation)
subj   <- erp_fs_nw |> distinct(SubjID, OS) |> filter(!is.na(OS))
os_m   <- mean(subj$OS)
os_sd  <- sd(subj$OS)
os_pts <- c(os_m - os_sd, os_m, os_m + os_sd)

# Some emmeans settings name the CI columns asymp.LCL / asymp.UCL; standardise them
fix_ci <- function(df) {
  names(df)[names(df) == "asymp.LCL"] <- "lower.CL"
  names(df)[names(df) == "asymp.UCL"] <- "upper.CL"
  df
}

# ---- Plot A: cell means at OS = -1 SD, mean, +1 SD ------------------------
emm_A <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity * family_size | OS,
                 at = list(OS = os_pts)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  fix_ci() |>
  mutate(OS_level = factor(OS, levels = os_pts,
                           labels = c("OS -1 SD", "OS mean", "OS +1 SD")),
         family_size = factor(family_size, levels = c("small", "large"),
                              labels = c("Small", "Large")),
         complexity  = factor(complexity, levels = c("simple", "complex"),
                              labels = c("Simple", "Complex")))

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.25)

  p_A <- ggplot(emm_A, aes(x = family_size, y = emmean,
                           colour = complexity, linetype = complexity, group = complexity)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_line(position = pd, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                  width = 0.12, position = pd, linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "solid") +
    geom_point(position = pd, size = 2.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ OS_level) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Simple = "#1b6ca8", Complex = "#d1495b")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Simple = "dashed", Complex = "solid")) +
    labs(x = "Family size", y = expression("Predicted N400 amplitude (" * mu * "V)"),
         colour = "Complexity", linetype = "Complexity") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
  # Add scale_y_reverse() if you want negative plotted up.
  
  p_A

# ---- Plot B: family size effect (Large - Small) across the observed OS range --
os_grid <- seq(min(subj$OS), max(subj$OS), length.out = 40)

emm_B <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ family_size | complexity * OS,
                 at = list(OS = os_grid)) |>
  contrast("revpairwise") |>          # large - small
  confint() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  fix_ci() |>
  mutate(complexity = factor(complexity, levels = c("simple", "complex"),
                             labels = c("Simple", "Complex")))

p_B <- ggplot(emm_B, aes(x = OS, y = estimate,
                         colour = complexity, fill = complexity, linetype = complexity)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = os_pts, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60")  +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), alpha = 0.18, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_rug(data = subj, aes(x = OS), inherit.aes = FALSE,
           sides = "b", alpha = 0.5, length = unit(0.02, "npc")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Simple = "#1b6ca8", Complex = "#d1495b")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c(Simple = "#1b6ca8", Complex = "#d1495b")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Simple = "dashed", Complex = "solid")) +
  labs(x = "Orthographic Sensitivity (PCA score)",
       y = expression("Family size effect, Large-Small (" * mu * "V)"),
       colour = "Complexity", fill = "Complexity", linetype = "Complexity") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

p_B

# ---- Save -------------------------------------------------------------------
ggsave("Figure_N400_CxFSxOS_cells.png", p_A, width = 7.5, height = 3.6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("Figure_N400_CxFSxOS_FSeffect.png", p_B, width = 5.5, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```

# Some emmeans settings name the CI columns asymp.LCL / asymp.UCL; standardise them

# ---- Plot A: cell means at LP = -1 SD, mean, +1 SD ------------------------
emm_A <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity * family_size | LP,

emm_B <- emmeans(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ family_size | complexity * LP,

TWO-WAY INTERACTIONS

There is no need to probe the two-way interactions separately. With ±0.5 coding and OS and LP centred, a two-way coefficient is that interaction averaged over the third factor. 
Complexity × LP (−0.143) is the LP slope of the complexity effect averaged over small- and large-family nonwords.

When Complexity × Family Size × LP is significant, that slope differs by family size, and the average can describe neither family size condition well.


```{r}
emtrends(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity | family_size, var = "LP") |> contrast("revpairwise")
emtrends(m_full_nw_n400_fs, ~ complexity | family_size, var = "OS") |> contrast("revpairwise")
```

                              at = list(OS = os_vals, LP = lp_vals[2]), nesting = NULL) |>
